name: Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. Masʿūd
summary: Author of Marāḥ al-arwāḥ, the last and fullest of the five books of ṣarf of the Ottoman madrasa; nothing more is known of his life.
bio: The sources tell nothing of his life: he is known only as the author of Marāḥ al-arwāḥ, and is thought to have died early in the 8th/14th century. His book, in seven chapters on the sound and the weak verbs, became the last of the five books of ṣarf that the Ottoman madrasa read before naḥw, and was printed again and again in Istanbul, Būlāq, Delhi and Lahore.
reception: Commented on by Shams al-Dīn Aḥmad, called Dikqoz (Dunqūz), by Badr al-Dīn al-ʿAynī (Malāḥ al-alwāḥ) and by Ibn Kemal (al-Falāḥ).
uncertain: His dates and his home are not known.
